In the Zimmermann PWA Kit repo (/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa), currently on branch `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`, there's a reported bug: the "was/now" sale-price display (showing a struck-through original/"was" price alongside a current/"now" price) is broken on mobile — it's causing the viewport to horizontally extend/overflow.

I need you to locate and report back on:

1. **The exact component that renders the was/now price pair.** Search for a component likely named something like `ZimmProductPrice`, or a price-rendering part inside `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/`. Read its full source. I already know `ZimmProductCardContent` composes it (via a `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` prop pair passed down from `ZimmProductCard`'s organism), and that there's a recent commit `0748af3` ("was/now sale price story for ProductCardContent") and `1fdb356` ("suppress known was-price contrast finding on new sale-price stories") — so the component and its Storybook story already exist. Find the exact file paths.

2. **Its full CSS recipe** (whether centralized in `overrides/app/theme/components/` or co-located as a `<name>.css.ts` beside the component) — read the whole thing. Pay close attention to: `whiteSpace`, `display`/`flex` direction, `width`/`minWidth`/`maxWidth`, `overflow`/`overflowWrap`/`wordBreak`, `flexShrink`, and whether there are separate mobile/desktop responsive rules (check for `DESKTOP_QUERY`/breakpoint media queries the way other recipes in this codebase use them — e.g. `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own breakpoint-based padding steps, mentioned in this codebase's docs).

3. **Every place this price component is actually composed/rendered** — grep for its import across `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` to find all consumers, and read how each one wraps/constrains it (container width, flex properties on the parent).

4. **Any existing Storybook story exercising a long/sale price on a narrow/mobile viewport** — check its `.stories.tsx` file for a mobile viewport-parameter story and whether it already shows (or was supposed to catch) this exact overflow.

5. **Check for any already-documented note about this specific issue** — grep the whole repo (`.claude/rules/`, `.docs/`, component docblocks) for anything mentioning "was/now", "sale price", or price overflow on mobile, in case this is a already partially-diagnosed known gap rather than something totally fresh.

Report back with: exact file paths and line numbers for the component + its CSS recipe, the full text of the relevant style properties (quote them, don't summarize vaguely), the list of consumers, and anything from the docs/story search. Do not propose a fix — I only need the facts so I can design one myself. Be thorough but keep the report organized and scannable.

    fix(ui-kits): suppress known was-price contrast finding on new sale-price stories (SFCC-236)
    
    CI's Storybook a11y check failed on both WithSalePrice stories added
    this session (ZimmProductCardContent and ZimmProductCard) with a
    color-contrast violation on the "was" price text.
    
    Not a new bug: the underlying colour is Figma's own design token
    (alias/color/text/subtlest, #969696), which genuinely fails WCAG AA
    contrast on white (2.95:1, needs 4.5:1) — confirmed via live Figma and
    git history. This exact trade-off was already hit and deliberately
    accepted during the original PRC-09 Was/Now implementation (Jersey
    Perez, SFCC-194): the team's own fix at the time was to keep the
    design-matching colour and suppress the automated check on the
    specific stories that render it (parameters: { a11y: { test: 'off' }
    }), not to change the colour. That decision predates this branch
    entirely and is untouched by it.
    
    These two new stories exercise the identical composed treatment but
    never carried the same suppression forward, so CI correctly re-caught
    the same already-accepted issue. Fixed by replicating the exact
    existing pattern (same parameters block, comment citing the same
    rationale) rather than revisiting the colour now.
    
    Verified locally with the same build->serve->test sequence CI uses
    (on an isolated port, not the developer's own running Storybook
    instance): all 44 story suites / 209 tests pass, including both
    previously-failing stories.

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { Link as RouteLink } from 'react-router-dom';
4	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
5	import { ZimmProductName } from '../../atoms/zimmProductName';
6	import { ZimmProductPrice } from '../../atoms/zimmProductPrice';
7	import { ZimmIcon } from '../../atoms/zimmIcon';
8	import { ZimmSizeChipGroup } from '../zimmSizeChipGroup';
9	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../zimmSizeChipGroup';
10	import { CARD_SLOT } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';
11	
12	/**
13	 * Selector contract for a later step (the ZimmProductCard organism, SFCC-236 Step 6): stable
14	 * `data-card-slot` values on this component's own DOM so that organism's own recipe can target
15	 * these descendants for hover-reveal styling without reaching into implementation details.
16	 * Do not rename these values without updating that recipe too — mirrors the same contract
17	 * `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` documents for its own slots:
18	 *   - "content"   — the outermost element (this component's root).
19	 *   - "price"     — the price wrapper. Always rendered regardless of variation; the organism's
20	 *                   own CSS is what shows/hides it on hover per variation (see the `showBag`/
21	 *                   `showSizeChips` props below), not this component.
22	 *   - "sizeChips" — the size-chip-group wrapper (present only when `showSizeChips` is true).
23	 *                   Always rendered in the DOM per Figma's `hidden=true` default on the "Size
24	 *                   Selector instance" node — the organism's hover-reveal CSS is what handles
25	 *                   visibility, not this component's own recipe (see zimmProductCardContent.css.ts).
26	 *   - "bag"       — the bag-button wrapper (present only when `showBag` is true). Added later
27	 *                   than the three above, for the organism's own mobile-breakpoint hide rule
28	 *                   (Figma: PLP/PDP's Mobile Card-content instances have the bag icon's `Icons`
29	 *                   frame `hidden="true"`; Desktop and Wishlist's own Mobile instance do not) — a
30	 *                   viewport-width concern, not a hover one, but the same
31	 *                   "this component always renders it, the organism's CSS decides visibility"
32	 *                   division of responsibility as the other slots.
33	 */
34	
35	// Same import base SFCC's own swatch-group/swatch.jsx uses for its `RouteLink`, and the same
36	// reasoning zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx already documents: a router `Link` delivers "URL updates
37	// without a full page reload" for real. Confirmed directly (no overrides/app/components/link/
38	// directory exists on disk) — there is no overrides/.../link equivalent to reuse instead.
39	const ProductNameLink = chakra(RouteLink);
40	
41	const messages = defineMessages({
42	  // Deliberately generic, not name-interpolated ("Add {name} to bag") — no such requirement was
43	  // given, and the visible product name already sits immediately to this button's left in the
44	  // same row, so the accessible name does not need to repeat it.
45	  addToBag: { id: 'product_card_content.bag.add_to_bag', defaultMessage: 'Add to bag' },
46	  // Figma node 40002163:41468 (Desktop, Hover, PLP/PDP, Unavailable=True) — an instance of the
47	  // shared CTA/Link atom (40001908:28374/40001908:28368) with its text swapped to "NOTIFY ME" in
48	  // this state. Authored here in sentence case, not literal caps, matching this codebase's
49	  // pattern of keeping translatable copy normal-case and letting the textStyle's CSS apply the
50	  // visual transform (see ZimmProductName's own normal-cased stories against `productNames`'
51	  // textTransform: 'uppercase') — `linkSm` was corrected to `textTransform: 'uppercase'` to
52	  // match (2026-09-03, theme/foundation/typography.ts), so this renders "NOTIFY ME" correctly.
53	  notifyMe: {
54	    id: 'product_card_content.notify_me.label',
55	    defaultMessage: 'Notify me',
56	  },
57	});
58	
59	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_CONTENT_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCardContent';
60	
61	/**
62	 * `ZimmProductName`'s own heading-level prop, read off the atom's real signature via a utility
63	 * type rather than a hand-typed duplicate union (typescript.md: "prefer utility types over
64	 * hand-rolled duplicate shapes... a hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
65	 * original changes"). Its type param is `'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'` — note this is NOT `'h2' | 'h3' |
66	 * 'h4'` as an earlier sketch of this component's contract assumed; see `headingLevel` below.
67	 */
68	type ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductName>['as'];
69	
70	export type ZimmProductCardContentProps = {
71	  /** The product's display name, rendered as the card's heading and link text. */
72	  name: string;
73	  /**
74	   * Heading level for the composed `ZimmProductName`, forwarded to it as `as`. Named
75	   * `headingLevel` here (rather than `as`) because this component is not itself polymorphic —
76	   * it always renders the same fixed element tree, it just hands the one real heading a level.

101	 * zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx's `Default` story already uses via its own `DefaultExample`.
102	 * Unlike that file, `ZimmProductCardContentProps` is a single flat type, not a discriminated
103	 * union keyed by `variation` — `selectedSizeChipValue`/`onSizeChipSelect` are already valid
104	 * (optional) members on every value of the type, so `{...args, selectedSizeChipValue,
105	 * onSizeChipSelect}` needs no narrowing before it assigns back to `ZimmProductCardContentProps`,
106	 * unlike that other file's `propsWithLiveSelection`. `handleSizeChipSelect` still fires the
107	 * original `args.onSizeChipSelect` (the `fn()` spy below) so Storybook's Actions panel keeps
108	 * logging the click.
109	 */
110	const WithSizeChipsExample = (args: ZimmProductCardContentProps) => {
111	  const [selectedSizeChipValue, setSelectedSizeChipValue] = useState<string | undefined>('m');
112	  const handleSizeChipSelect = (value: string) => {
113	    setSelectedSizeChipValue(value);
114	    args.onSizeChipSelect?.(value);
115	  };
116	  return (
117	    <ZimmProductCardContent
118	      {...args}
119	      selectedSizeChipValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
120	      onSizeChipSelect={handleSizeChipSelect}
121	    />
122	  );
123	};
124	
125	/** PLP-shaped: the size-chip picker renders in place of the attributes line. Size chips are
126	 *  genuinely interactive here, not a static snapshot — starts pre-selected at 'M'; click a
127	 *  different chip to see the live selection move. Rendered via `WithSizeChipsExample` above,
128	 *  which owns `selectedSizeChipValue` as local state; every other arg below is unchanged. */
129	export const WithSizeChips: Story = {
130	  args: {
131	    ...Default.args,
132	    showSizeChips: true,
133	    sizeChipValues: SIZES,
134	    selectedSizeChipValue: 'm',
135	    onSizeChipSelect: fn(),
136	  },
137	  render: (args) => <WithSizeChipsExample {...args} />,
138	};
139	
140	/**
141	 * PLP-shaped, one-size product: triggers `ZimmSizeChipGroup`'s own `values.length === 1` branch
142	 * (see that component's `index.tsx`), which renders a single non-interactive label rather than a
143	 * `[role=radiogroup]` of chips. Plain args here, not wrapped in `WithSizeChipsExample` and with no
144	 * `selectedSizeChipValue`/`onSizeChipSelect` — there is nothing to select in that branch (it never
145	 * reaches the chip-click/keyboard-navigation code path at all), so the interactive wrapper this
146	 * file uses for `WithSizeChips` would misleadingly imply a selection state that doesn't exist here.
147	 */
148	export const WithSizeChipsOneSize: Story = {
149	  args: {
150	    ...Default.args,
151	    showSizeChips: true,
152	    sizeChipValues: [{ value: 'os', label: 'One size' }],
153	  },
154	};
155	
156	/** Out-of-stock: the bag button is present but disabled, and the notify-me CTA takes its place
157	 *  as the available action. */
158	export const Unavailable: Story = {
159	  args: {
160	    ...Default.args,
161	    isUnavailable: true,
162	    showNotifyMe: true,
163	    onNotifyMe: fn(),
164	  },
165	};
166	
167	/** A variant re-fetch in progress — ZimmProductPrice renders its own invisible placeholder,
168	 *  preserving the layout slot rather than collapsing it. */
169	export const LoadingPrice: Story = {
170	  args: {
171	    ...Default.args,
172	    currentPrice: undefined,
173	    isPriceLoading: true,
174	  },
175	};

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { useHistory } from 'react-router-dom';
4	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
5	import { ZimmProductCardMedia } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
6	import type { ZimmProductCardMediaImage } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
7	import { ZimmProductCardContent } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardContent';
8	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../../molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';
9	
10	/**
11	 * SFCC-236 Step 6 — the organism that assembles Step 4's `ZimmProductCardMedia` and Step 5's
12	 * `ZimmProductCardContent` into the full product card, across the three confirmed variations.
13	 * Figma component set `Product-card`, node `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size x State x Type x
14	 * Unavailable), file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`. The variation matrix below reflects the resolved
15	 * `hidden`-attribute reading confirmed against the real assembled Card-content instances:
16	 *
17	 *   Home      (40000214:6141 default / 40002163:36593 hover)   — image + name only by default;
18	 *             bag/attributes/size-selector hidden always; a hover-CAPABLE pointer reveals price
19	 *             on hover. Mobile (`40000223:2821`) shows price unconditionally instead — it has no
20	 *             Hover variant at all, so a price hidden "by default, revealed on hover" like the
21	 *             original build shipped would never be revealed there at all (Fix E, found in the
22	 *             full-sweep follow-up audit; confirmed live as a real bug, not just a Figma reading).
23	 *             Arrows appear on hover-capable pointers regardless of variation (Media's own
24	 *             concern, driven purely by image count).
25	 *   PLP/PDP   (40002163:41441 default / 40002163:41459 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
26	 *             price by default, no attributes, size-selector hidden; hover hides price and
27	 *             reveals the size-selector in its place; arrows appear.
28	 *   Wishlist  (40002187:58446 default / 40002187:58458 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
29	 *             attributes (colour+size) + price by default, size-selector hidden; hover hides
30	 *             price and reveals the size-selector, confirmed identical to PLP's own hover reveal
31	 *             via node `40002187:58460` (the Wishlist hover instance carries no `hidden`
32	 *             attribute on "Size Selector" at all) — this is NOT what the SFCC-236 Jira AC text
33	 *             says (it only mentions the image switch + arrows for Wishlist hover). It shipped
34	 *             matching the design anyway — a judgment call made during implementation, not a
35	 *             conflict that was raised on the ticket or separately ratified.
36	 *
37	 * "Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly
38	 * like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.
39	 *
40	 * Unavailable=True (Fix C, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) is confirmed designed for **every**
41	 * variation, not just `plp` — an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed the opposite, before
42	 * the Default+Hover Unavailable instances for `home` (40002163:39981 / :39990) and `wishlist`
43	 * (40002187:58452 / :58464) were actually checked. The confirmed rule, identical across all three:
44	 *   - The PLP/Wishlist size-selector hover-swap is suppressed entirely when unavailable — nothing
45	 *     to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced
46	 *     (`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` are both AND-ed with `!isUnavailable` below).
47	 *     Home's own hover-reveals-price behaviour is unaffected — its Unavailable Hover reference
48	 *     still reveals price exactly as the in-stock case does.
49	 *   - "Notify me" is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default, revealed on
50	 *     hover/focus-visible, confirmed via every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference) but
51	 *     unconditionally visible on touch (confirmed via the Mobile Unavailable references —
52	 *     Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so whatever they show is the only state a touch
53	 *     pointer ever sees, and all of them show notify-me plainly).
54	 * `isUnavailable` and `onNotifyMe` are threaded through uniformly to `ZimmProductCardContent`
55	 * (the only one of the two composed children with an `isUnavailable` concept at all —
56	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` has no such prop); this organism does not itself restrict `showNotifyMe`
57	 * to any one variation — a caller that never passes `onNotifyMe` simply gets no notify-me button.
58	 *
59	 * Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit, after the above was already built and approved): the
60	 * Desktop-only "price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover" behaviour above is NOT what
61	 * Mobile does. Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`) both have
62	 * `Price` `hidden="true"` and only "Notify me" visible — a genuine SWAP, unlike Desktop's additive
63	 * treatment — where Mobile Home Unavailable (`40002163:41204`) keeps price visible alongside
64	 * notify-me, unchanged from Desktop. `sizeSelectorUnavailable` (already computed below for the
65	 * size-chip permanent-hide) drives this too, in zimmProductCard.css.ts, since it is already
66	 * exactly "PLP/Wishlist and unavailable" — the same condition, no new variable needed.
67	 *
68	 * The bag icon also has two Mobile-breakpoint hides, both viewport-width concerns unrelated to
69	 * hover capability (see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rules, keyed off the same
70	 * `breakpoints` token `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` already uses for its padding steps):
71	 *   - `hideBagOnMobile` — PLP only, unconditional. Figma's Mobile PLP/PDP Card-content instances
72	 *     (`40002163:41479` available / `40002163:41488` unavailable) both have the bag icon's
73	 *     `Icons` frame `hidden="true"` regardless of stock status, where Desktop's own PLP instance
74	 *     leaves it visible.
75	 *   - `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` (Fix G, same follow-up audit) — Wishlist only, and only
76	 *     when unavailable. Wishlist's Mobile instance shows the bag when available
77	 *     (`40002187:58470`) and hides it only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
78	 *     PLP's own unconditional rule, so it needs its own flag rather than reusing
79	 *     `hideBagOnMobile`. `index.tsx` combines both into one `bagHiddenOnMobile` boolean before
80	 *     the recipe ever sees it — the recipe only needs "hide this on mobile for this render", not
81	 *     which of the two reasons applies.
82	 *
83	 * KNOWN GAP: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s `priority` prop (its LCP eager-load escape hatch) has no
84	 * passthrough here — every card composed via this organism lazy-loads its primary image. Not in
85	 * the given component contract for this step; flagged rather than added silently, since a PLP
86	 * page placing this organism above the fold would want it.
87	 *
88	 * Badge (feature addition, not a "Fix" like the ones above — the underlying design gap was
89	 * genuinely closed, not misread): `ZimmProductCardContent`'s docblock used to claim no Figma
90	 * design existed for SFCC-236's badge AC. It does — the "Tag" overlay, confirmed present and
91	 * pixel-identical on every Size/Type variant checked (nodes 40002163:41442, 40002096:12223,
92	 * 40002187:58447, 40002163:41478, 40004599:89266, 40004638:120485) — it was just nested one
93	 * level deeper (inside "Image Group", i.e. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain) than the first pass
94	 * looked. Per Dani Rivett's scope note on the ticket, the badge shows on PLP and Wishlist (and
95	 * therefore Recently Viewed Full History, which already reuses the `plp` variation) and is
96	 * suppressed on Home — driven by `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge` below, the same table-driven
97	 * mechanism as every other variation decision in this file. Figma's own Home node still shows
98	 * the Tag layer un-hidden, contradicting that scope note — treating the confirmed written
99	 * requirement as authoritative over the file's possibly-stale layer visibility here, flagged
100	 * rather than silently picked.
101	 *
102	 * Badge count (confirmed after the above shipped, via a Dev Mode Connect Note on the separate
103	 * "Product Cards" Figma file — QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs, node 3448:35976 — distinct from the
104	 * design-system component-set file cited throughout this docblock): "only 1 product badge will
105	 * show up on these product cards - depending on the configured hierarchy, the highest priority
106	 * badge will be shown," with that priority logic owned by SFCC-225. This confirms `badge?:
107	 * string` (a single value, not a list) is the correct, final shape for this prop — not a
108	 * placeholder pending a possible future move to an array. SFCC-225's own already-merged SCAPI
109	 * hook writes `c_productBadges` as an array sorted by `badgePriorityOrder`, so whatever mapper
110	 * eventually feeds this prop (none exists yet — no page consumes this organism) just needs
111	 * `c_productBadges[0]?.productBadge`, not any re-sorting of its own.
112	 *
113	 * Hover image-swap on Home (same Dani-vs-AC contradiction as the Badge note above, resolved the
114	 * same direction): Dani's comment also says "we don't want the hover action (model photo) on
115	 * the homepage," but the AC update three days later frames the tile-image hover-swap as an
116	 * unconditional Core Component behaviour with no Home exclusion — and the code as first shipped
117	 * followed the AC, passing `swapOnHover` to `ZimmProductCardMedia` unconditionally with no
118	 * variation gate at all. Treated the comment as more authoritative than the AC text here too:
119	 * `VARIATION_CONFIG.showHoverImageSwap` now suppresses the swap for `home` specifically. This
120	 * is unrelated to, and does not affect, Home's own
121	 * `hoverRevealsPrice` — that is a separate mechanism (a style flag consumed by this organism's
122	 * own recipe), not `swapOnHover`.
123	 *
124	 * KNOWN GAP (postbuild doc/traceability audit, comment-only — no behaviour change): both
125	 * quotes above, from Dani's scope note (Jira comment 13880 on SFCC-236), truncate at the same
126	 * point. In full, her instruction is no badge and no hover-image-swap on "the Homepage or on
127	 * the Recently Viewed product carousel" — the Badge note above and this Hover image-swap note
128	 * each only implement and discuss the Homepage half. The Recently Viewed carousel half has no
129	 * code path in this file today: that surface is SFCC-83's rail component, which does not exist
130	 * yet and has no entry in the `ZimmProductCardVariation` union above. A rail caller reaching
131	 * for the closest existing option, `variation: 'plp'`, would get `showBadge: true` and
132	 * `showHoverImageSwap: true` from `VARIATION_CONFIG` — the opposite of what Dani asked for on
133	 * that surface. Whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to either add a dedicated `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry
134	 * for the rail (both flags `false`) or get explicit written confirmation on the ticket that the
135	 * suppression doesn't apply there — not assume `'plp'` already covers it.
136	 *
137	 * Fix I (SFCC-236, found via live mobile-device testing on this branch, same round that found
138	 * Fix H): multi-image cards did not respond to a real touch swipe at all — the slide indicator
139	 * rendered correctly (so the image data/gallery logic was fine), but swiping the image never
140	 * paged it. Root cause and CSS fix are `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s own Fix I (docblock point 2):
141	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` was the one interactive region never lifted above the stretched-link
142	 * overlay, so a swipe gesture starting on the image landed on the invisible overlay `<a>` first
143	 * and never reached the real scroll container underneath. Lifting Media above the overlay fixes
144	 * the swipe, but has a side effect: a plain tap/click on the image used to "work" by landing on
145	 * that same overlay and navigating to the PDP — once Media sits on top, the tap no longer reaches
146	 * it, and Media itself had no click behaviour of its own. `handleMediaClick` below restores that
147	 * navigation deliberately, via `useHistory().push(href)` rather than depending on the overlay by
148	 * accident: this repo is pinned to react-router-dom v5.3.4 (`package.json`), which has no
149	 * `useNavigate` — `useHistory()` + `history.push()` is the correct v5 primitive, already
150	 * established in this codebase (`footer/index.tsx`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`,
151	 * `pages/product-detail/index.tsx`) and the same one the base SFCC `product-list` page itself
152	 * uses. `href` needed no new prop plumbing — this organism already destructures it from its own
153	 * base props (above) and previously only forwarded it to `ZimmProductCardContent`. The handler
154	 * guards against the two arrow buttons and the remove/close button — all real `<button>`
155	 * descendants of `ZimmProductCardMedia` — via `(event.target as HTMLElement).closest('button')`,
156	 * so paging and `onRemove` keep firing on their own and never also navigate. No custom drag-vs-tap
157	 * detection is needed for the swipe/tap split itself: browsers natively suppress the synthetic
158	 * `click` event after a real drag/scroll on the same element, so a swipe pages the gallery without
159	 * ever reaching this handler, while a plain tap (no movement) still fires it exactly as the old
160	 * overlay click did.
161	 */
162	
163	/** Re-exported under this organism's own name so a page-level caller never has to reach into a
164	 *  molecule's type — the shape itself is Media's own `ZimmProductCardMediaImage`, not a
165	 *  redeclaration (a hand-copied duplicate would silently drift from its source). */
166	export type ZimmProductCardImage = ZimmProductCardMediaImage;
167	
168	/** `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own already-derived heading-level type (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`,
169	 *  itself derived from `ZimmProductName`'s `as` prop) — read via `ComponentProps` off the
170	 *  component this organism actually forwards it to, rather than a hand-typed duplicate union. */
171	type ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductCardContent>['headingLevel'];
172	
173	/**
174	 * Exported alongside `ZimmProductCardProps` (not just kept module-private) so a test/fixture can
175	 * build a properly *narrowed* per-variation props object — e.g.
176	 * `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation` — instead of a value typed as the
177	 * full union. This matters for real, not just for convenience: TypeScript's excess-property
178	 * check on a *union* target is weak (a property valid on any one member is not flagged as excess
179	 * on a fresh literal discriminated toward a different member), so proving "the wishlist-only
180	 * fields don't exist on Home" needs an assignment to Home's own narrow shape specifically, not to
181	 * the union alias — see index.test.tsx's `@ts-expect-error` cases and its overloaded
182	 * `buildCardProps` helper.
183	 */
184	export type ZimmProductCardBaseProps = {
185	  /** Stable per-card identifier. Not used for any layout/behavioural decision — exposed as a
186	   *  `data-product-id` attribute on the root element as a DOM hook for QA automation/analytics,
187	   *  the same kind of caller-facing marker `data-testid` already serves in this build's other
188	   *  components, without overloading that attribute's own testing-only convention. */
189	  id: string;
190	  /** PDP destination, pre-site-prefixed by the caller — forwarded straight to
191	   *  `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own `href` (see that component's own JSDoc on trust level). */
192	  href: string;
193	  name: string;
194	  headingLevel: ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel;
195	  primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage;
196	  hoverImage?: ZimmProductCardImage;
197	  images?: ZimmProductCardImage[];
198	  currentPrice?: string;
199	  originalPrice?: string;
200	  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
201	  isUnavailable?: boolean;
202	  /** Only meaningful when `isUnavailable` is true. See the module docblock for why this is not
203	   *  restricted to the `plp` variation at the type level. */
204	  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
205	  /**
206	   * Merchandiser-configured badge label (e.g. "Runway", "Exclusive"). Always a single value —
207	   * confirmed via a Figma Dev Mode Connect Note that only the single highest-priority badge is
208	   * ever shown, never a list (see the module docblock's "Badge count" note). Not restricted to
209	   * any variation at the type level, same reasoning as `onNotifyMe` above — whether it actually
210	   * renders is `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge`'s job (PLP/Wishlist show it, Home suppresses it; see
211	   * the module docblock's "Badge" note).
212	   */
213	  badge?: string;
214	};
215	
216	export type ZimmProductCardPlpVariation = {
217	  variation: 'plp';
218	  onAddToBag?: () => void;
219	  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
220	  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
221	  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
222	};
223	
224	export type ZimmProductCardHomeVariation = {
225	  variation: 'home';
226	  // No additions — Home never shows the bag, attributes, or size chips (see VARIATION_CONFIG).
227	};
228	
229	export type ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation = {
230	  variation: 'wishlist';
231	  /** Required, not optional — the Wishlist AC always shows the attributes line. */
232	  colour: string;
233	  size: string;
234	  /** Required — a wishlist card with no way to remove itself is a spec violation. */
235	  onRemove: () => void;
236	  /** Bag is always visible for Wishlist per the confirmed matrix above. */
237	  onAddToBag?: () => void;
238	  /** Same trio `ZimmProductCardPlpVariation` declares, and for the same reason: confirmed via the
239	   *  real Figma Wishlist Hover instance (node 40002187:58458) during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual
240	   *  audit that Wishlist's hover reveal is a genuine, populated size-selector swap identical to
241	   *  PLP's — not a PLP-only affordance. `index.tsx`'s render body already forwarded these
242	   *  unconditionally to `ZimmProductCardContent` for every variation (via the
243	   *  `ZimmProductCardVariationFields` cast below); this type previously just didn't expose them
244	   *  to a Wishlist caller, which is what let the Wishlist story ship without ever populating them. */
245	  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
246	  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
247	  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
248	};
249	
250	export type ZimmProductCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps &
251	  (ZimmProductCardPlpVariation | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation);
252	
253	type ZimmProductCardVariation =
254	  | ZimmProductCardPlpVariation['variation']
255	  | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation['variation']
256	  | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation['variation'];
257	
258	/**
259	 * Widened, not narrowed: every variation-specific field is optional here regardless of which
260	 * branch is actually active, purely so the component body below can destructure once with no
261	 * `if`/`switch` on `props.variation` — the extensibility AC requires every layout/visibility
262	 * decision to come from `VARIATION_CONFIG`, keyed by the discriminant, never a branching
263	 * statement. The exported `ZimmProductCardProps` discriminated union above is what actually
264	 * enforces correct usage at every call site (proven by the `@ts-expect-error` cases in
265	 * index.test.tsx) — this cast only relaxes internal access inside this file; it changes nothing
266	 * about what a caller may legally pass in.
267	 */
268	type ZimmProductCardVariationFields = Partial<
269	  Omit<ZimmProductCardPlpVariation, 'variation'> &
270	    Omit<ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation, 'variation'> &
271	    Omit<ZimmProductCardHomeVariation, 'variation'>
272	>;
273	
274	type ZimmProductCardVariationConfig = {
275	  showBag: boolean;
276	  showAttributes: boolean;
277	  showSizeChips: boolean;
278	  /** PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default and hides on hover. */
279	  hoverHidesPrice: boolean;
280	  /** Home only: price is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
281	  hoverRevealsPrice: boolean;
282	  /** PLP/Wishlist: the size-chip picker is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
283	  hoverRevealsSizeSelector: boolean;
284	  showRemove: boolean;
285	  /** PLP only (found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): Figma's Mobile Card-content
286	   *  instance has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`, unlike Desktop and unlike
287	   *  Wishlist's own Mobile instance (bag stays visible there on every breakpoint). A viewport-
288	   *  width concern, not a hover one — see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rule. */
289	  hideBagOnMobile: boolean;
290	  /** Wishlist only (found during the follow-up full-sweep visual audit against every variant x
291	   *  state node): unlike PLP's unconditional `hideBagOnMobile`, Wishlist's Mobile Card-content
292	   *  instance shows the bag icon when available (`40002187:58470`) and hides it
293	   *  (`Icons` frame `hidden="true"`) only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
294	   *  `hideBagOnMobile`, and combined with it (not replacing it) in the `bagHiddenOnMobile`
295	   *  derivation below, since the two are mutually exclusive per variation today but there is no
296	   *  reason to assume that stays true forever. */
297	  hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: boolean;
298	  /** Shown on PLP/Wishlist, suppressed on Home — see the module docblock's "Badge" note. */
299	  showBadge: boolean;
300	  /**
301	   * Allows `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s primary/hover image crossfade for this variation. Suppressed
302	   * on Home per Dani Rivett's scope note, overriding the AC's unconditional framing — see the
303	   * module docblock's "Hover image-swap on Home" note. `false` here means a supplied
304	   * `hoverImage` is simply never swapped to, regardless of pointer capability.
305	   */
306	  showHoverImageSwap: boolean;
307	};
308	
309	/**
310	 * The extensibility AC's actual mechanism: every layout/visibility decision this organism makes
311	 * reads from this table, keyed by `variation` — adding a future variation means adding a union
312	 * member above and one row here, touching no JSX. `index.tsx`'s render body contains no
313	 * `switch`/`if` on `props.variation` anywhere (verify with
314	 * `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` — zero hits).
315	 */
316	const VARIATION_CONFIG: Record<ZimmProductCardVariation, ZimmProductCardVariationConfig> = {
317	  home: {
318	    showBag: false,
319	    showAttributes: false,
320	    showSizeChips: false,
321	    hoverHidesPrice: false,
322	    hoverRevealsPrice: true,
323	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: false,
324	    showRemove: false,
325	    hideBagOnMobile: false,
326	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
327	    showBadge: false,
328	    showHoverImageSwap: false,
329	  },
330	  plp: {
331	    showBag: true,
332	    showAttributes: false,
333	    showSizeChips: true,
334	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
335	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
336	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
337	    showRemove: false,
338	    hideBagOnMobile: true,
339	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
340	    showBadge: true,
341	    showHoverImageSwap: true,
342	  },
343	  wishlist: {
344	    showBag: true,
345	    showAttributes: true,
346	    showSizeChips: true,
347	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
348	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
349	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
350	    showRemove: true,
351	    hideBagOnMobile: false,
352	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: true,
353	    showBadge: true,
354	    showHoverImageSwap: true,
355	  },
356	};
357	
358	const messages = defineMessages({
359	  // Interpolated with the product name, matching ZimmProductPrice's WAS/NOW pattern — Media's
360	  // own `removeLabel` prop is a plain string, so the interpolation happens here, at the one call
361	  // site that actually knows the product name.
362	  removeFromWishlist: {
363	    id: 'product_card.remove.from_wishlist',
364	    defaultMessage: 'Remove {name} from wishlist',
365	  },
366	});
367	
368	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCard';
369	
370	/**
371	 * Organism — the full product card, composing `ZimmProductCardMedia` and `ZimmProductCardContent`
372	 * across the `home` / `plp` / `wishlist` variations. See the module docblock above for the
373	 * confirmed Figma variation matrix and this component's own recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) for
374	 * the stretched-link and hover-reveal mechanics that live entirely in CSS, not in this render
375	 * body — both children are always rendered in full, with every one of their own sub-parts; CSS
376	 * alone decides what is visible for a given variation and pointer capability.
377	 *
378	 * @param props see `ZimmProductCardProps` — a discriminated union on `variation`.
379	 */
380	export const ZimmProductCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
381	  const {
382	    id,
383	    href,
384	    name,
385	    headingLevel,
386	    primaryImage,
387	    hoverImage,
388	    images,
389	    currentPrice,
390	    originalPrice,
391	    isPriceLoading,
392	    isUnavailable,
393	    onNotifyMe,
394	    badge,
395	    variation,
396	  } = props;
397	
398	  const { onAddToBag, sizeChipValues, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect, colour, size, onRemove } =
399	    props as ZimmProductCardVariationFields;
400	
401	  const intl = useIntl();
402	  const history = useHistory();
403	  const config = VARIATION_CONFIG[variation];
404	
405	  // Both conditions required — an organism that sets isUnavailable without a real callback
406	  // should not show a dead notify-me button. Mirrors ZimmProductCardContent's own
407	  // showNotifyMeButton co-requirement.
408	  const showNotifyMe = Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
409	
410	  // Fix C (SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): confirmed against the real Figma Default+Hover
411	  // instances for every variation × Unavailable=True (including the Mobile/no-hover variants,
412	  // which show the only state a touch pointer ever sees) that `isUnavailable` suppresses the
413	  // size-selector hover-swap entirely — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so
414	  // price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own hover-reveals-price
415	  // behaviour is untouched by this — Home's Unavailable Hover reference (node 40002163:39990)
416	  // still reveals price on hover exactly as the in-stock case does; only the PLP/Wishlist
417	  // hide-and-swap needs suppressing.
418	  //
419	  // Suppressing `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` alone is not enough to reproduce that reference: it
420	  // only stops the organism adding its OWN hide/reveal pair, which leaves the size-chip wrapper
421	  // at Content's own natural (visible) default — briefly shipped that way mid-fix and caught by
422	  // re-checking the real Storybook render against Figma, which confirms size chips stay hidden
423	  // in BOTH states when unavailable, not just "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
424	  // carries that permanent hide separately, unconditional (not gated by hover-capability at all —
425	  // this isn't a pointer-type concern, unlike everything else in this recipe).
426	  //
427	  // Follow-up (full-sweep visual audit against every variant x state node, not just the sampled
428	  // set the first pass checked): `sizeSelectorUnavailable` ALSO drives a mobile-only price hide
429	  // in the recipe now (Fix F) — confirmed via `get_metadata` that Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable
430	  // hide price and show notify-me in its place (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`), the OPPOSITE
431	  // of Desktop's additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover). Nothing
432	  // extra is computed here for it — the recipe reads the same `sizeSelectorUnavailable` boolean
433	  // for both the size-chip permanent-hide and this new price rule, since both only ever apply to
434	  // the same PLP/Wishlist-and-unavailable case.
435	  const hoverHidesPrice = config.hoverHidesPrice && !isUnavailable;
436	  const hoverRevealsSizeSelector = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && !isUnavailable;
437	  const sizeSelectorUnavailable = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && Boolean(isUnavailable);
438	
439	  // Fix G (same follow-up audit): Wishlist-only. `hideBagOnMobile` alone only covers PLP's own
440	  // unconditional mobile hide; Wishlist's bag stays visible on mobile UNLESS unavailable
441	  // (`40002187:58470` vs `40002187:58473`). Combined into one boolean here rather than exposing
442	  // both conditions to the recipe — it only needs to know "hide this on mobile for this render",
443	  // not why.
444	  const bagHiddenOnMobile = config.hideBagOnMobile || (config.hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable && Boolean(isUnavailable));
445	
446	  const removeLabel = config.showRemove ? intl.formatMessage(messages.removeFromWishlist, { name }) : undefined;
447	  const resolvedBadge = config.showBadge ? badge : undefined;
448	
449	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE, {
450	    hoverHidesPrice,
451	    hoverRevealsPrice: config.hoverRevealsPrice,
452	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
453	    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
454	    // Same Fix C audit: notify-me is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default,
455	    // revealed on hover/focus-visible — every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it
456	    // appearing only there) but unconditionally visible on touch (every Mobile Unavailable
457	    // reference — the only state a touch pointer ever sees, per the "Mobile has no Hover variant"
458	    // finding — shows it plainly, with no hover to reveal it). This flag is deliberately keyed off
459	    // `showNotifyMe` itself, not `variation`: the confirmed behaviour is identical across all
460	    // three variations, and the recipe's selector simply matches nothing when notify-me isn't
461	    // mounted at all.
462	    hoverRevealsNotifyMe: showNotifyMe,
463	    hideBagOnMobile: bagHiddenOnMobile,
464	  });
465	
466	  // Fix I — see the module docblock's own "Fix I" paragraph for the full narrative. Guards the
467	  // two arrow buttons and the remove/close button (all real <button> descendants of
468	  // ZimmProductCardMedia) so paging/onRemove keep firing on their own and never also navigate.
469	  // Fix L (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a real <a> lets the
470	  // browser handle Cmd/Ctrl-click (new tab), Shift-click (new window), and non-primary-button
471	  // clicks natively — this handler only ever replaces the in-page navigation an UNMODIFIED,
472	  // primary-button click used to reach via the stretched-link overlay (see Fix I). Bailing out on
473	  // any of those instead of forcing an in-tab `history.push` regardless of what the shopper
474	  // actually asked for; a no-op here is a real gap (it doesn't open a new tab the way a real link
475	  // would) but is strictly better than silently overriding an explicit "open elsewhere" signal.
476	  const handleMediaClick = (event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>): void => {
477	    const target = event.target as HTMLElement;
478	    if (target.closest('button')) return;
479	    if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.shiftKey || event.altKey || event.button !== 0) return;
480	    history.push(href);
481	  };
482	
483	  return (
484	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-testid="product-card" data-product-id={id}>
485	      <ZimmProductCardMedia
486	        primaryImage={primaryImage}
487	        hoverImage={hoverImage}
488	        images={images}
489	        swapOnHover={config.showHoverImageSwap && Boolean(hoverImage)}
490	        showControls
491	        badge={resolvedBadge}
492	        onRemove={onRemove}
493	        removeLabel={removeLabel}
494	        onClick={handleMediaClick}
495	      />
496	      <ZimmProductCardContent
497	        name={name}
498	        headingLevel={headingLevel}
499	        href={href}
500	        currentPrice={currentPrice}
501	        originalPrice={originalPrice}
502	        isPriceLoading={isPriceLoading}
503	        showAttributes={config.showAttributes}
504	        colour={colour}
505	        size={size}
506	        showBag={config.showBag}
507	        isUnavailable={isUnavailable}
508	        onAddToBag={onAddToBag}
509	        showSizeChips={config.showSizeChips}
510	        sizeChipValues={sizeChipValues}
511	        selectedSizeChipValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
512	        onSizeChipSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
513	        showNotifyMe={showNotifyMe}
514	        onNotifyMe={onNotifyMe}
515	      />
516	    </chakra.div>
517	  );
518	};
519	
520	export default ZimmProductCard;
521

import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { useHistory } from 'react-router-dom';
import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
import { ZimmProductCardMedia } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
import type { ZimmProductCardMediaImage } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
import { ZimmProductCardContent } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardContent';
import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../../molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';

/**
 * SFCC-236 Step 6 — the organism that assembles Step 4's `ZimmProductCardMedia` and Step 5's
 * `ZimmProductCardContent` into the full product card, across the three confirmed variations.
 * Figma component set `Product-card`, node `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size x State x Type x
 * Unavailable), file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`. The variation matrix below reflects the resolved
 * `hidden`-attribute reading confirmed against the real assembled Card-content instances:
 *
 *   Home      (40000214:6141 default / 40002163:36593 hover)   — image + name only by default;
 *             bag/attributes/size-selector hidden always; a hover-CAPABLE pointer reveals price
 *             on hover. Mobile (`40000223:2821`) shows price unconditionally instead — it has no
 *             Hover variant at all, so a price hidden "by default, revealed on hover" like the
 *             original build shipped would never be revealed there at all (Fix E, found in the
 *             full-sweep follow-up audit; confirmed live as a real bug, not just a Figma reading).
 *             Arrows appear on hover-capable pointers regardless of variation (Media's own
 *             concern, driven purely by image count).
 *   PLP/PDP   (40002163:41441 default / 40002163:41459 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
 *             price by default, no attributes, size-selector hidden; hover hides price and
 *             reveals the size-selector in its place; arrows appear.
 *   Wishlist  (40002187:58446 default / 40002187:58458 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
 *             attributes (colour+size) + price by default, size-selector hidden; hover hides
 *             price and reveals the size-selector, confirmed identical to PLP's own hover reveal
 *             via node `40002187:58460` (the Wishlist hover instance carries no `hidden`
 *             attribute on "Size Selector" at all) — this is NOT what the SFCC-236 Jira AC text
 *             says (it only mentions the image switch + arrows for Wishlist hover). It shipped
 *             matching the design anyway — a judgment call made during implementation, not a
 *             conflict that was raised on the ticket or separately ratified.
 *
 * "Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly
 * like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.
 *
 * Unavailable=True (Fix C, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) is confirmed designed for **every**
 * variation, not just `plp` — an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed the opposite, before
 * the Default+Hover Unavailable instances for `home` (40002163:39981 / :39990) and `wishlist`
 * (40002187:58452 / :58464) were actually checked. The confirmed rule, identical across all three:
 *   - The PLP/Wishlist size-selector hover-swap is suppressed entirely when unavailable — nothing
 *     to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced
 *     (`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` are both AND-ed with `!isUnavailable` below).
 *     Home's own hover-reveals-price behaviour is unaffected — its Unavailable Hover reference
 *     still reveals price exactly as the in-stock case does.
 *   - "Notify me" is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default, revealed on
 *     hover/focus-visible, confirmed via every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference) but
 *     unconditionally visible on touch (confirmed via the Mobile Unavailable references —
 *     Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so whatever they show is the only state a touch
 *     pointer ever sees, and all of them show notify-me plainly).
 * `isUnavailable` and `onNotifyMe` are threaded through uniformly to `ZimmProductCardContent`
 * (the only one of the two composed children with an `isUnavailable` concept at all —
 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` has no such prop); this organism does not itself restrict `showNotifyMe`
 * to any one variation — a caller that never passes `onNotifyMe` simply gets no notify-me button.
 *
 * Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit, after the above was already built and approved): the
 * Desktop-only "price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover" behaviour above is NOT what
 * Mobile does. Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`) both have
 * `Price` `hidden="true"` and only "Notify me" visible — a genuine SWAP, unlike Desktop's additive
 * treatment — where Mobile Home Unavailable (`40002163:41204`) keeps price visible alongside
 * notify-me, unchanged from Desktop. `sizeSelectorUnavailable` (already computed below for the
 * size-chip permanent-hide) drives this too, in zimmProductCard.css.ts, since it is already
 * exactly "PLP/Wishlist and unavailable" — the same condition, no new variable needed.
 *
 * The bag icon also has two Mobile-breakpoint hides, both viewport-width concerns unrelated to
 * hover capability (see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rules, keyed off the same
 * `breakpoints` token `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` already uses for its padding steps):
 *   - `hideBagOnMobile` — PLP only, unconditional. Figma's Mobile PLP/PDP Card-content instances
 *     (`40002163:41479` available / `40002163:41488` unavailable) both have the bag icon's
 *     `Icons` frame `hidden="true"` regardless of stock status, where Desktop's own PLP instance
 *     leaves it visible.
 *   - `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` (Fix G, same follow-up audit) — Wishlist only, and only
 *     when unavailable. Wishlist's Mobile instance shows the bag when available
 *     (`40002187:58470`) and hides it only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
 *     PLP's own unconditional rule, so it needs its own flag rather than reusing
 *     `hideBagOnMobile`. `index.tsx` combines both into one `bagHiddenOnMobile` boolean before
 *     the recipe ever sees it — the recipe only needs "hide this on mobile for this render", not
 *     which of the two reasons applies.
 *
 * KNOWN GAP: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s `priority` prop (its LCP eager-load escape hatch) has no
 * passthrough here — every card composed via this organism lazy-loads its primary image. Not in
 * the given component contract for this step; flagged rather than added silently, since a PLP
 * page placing this organism above the fold would want it.
 *
 * Badge (feature addition, not a "Fix" like the ones above — the underlying design gap was
 * genuinely closed, not misread): `ZimmProductCardContent`'s docblock used to claim no Figma
 * design existed for SFCC-236's badge AC. It does — the "Tag" overlay, confirmed present and
 * pixel-identical on every Size/Type variant checked (nodes 40002163:41442, 40002096:12223,
 * 40002187:58447, 40002163:41478, 40004599:89266, 40004638:120485) — it was just nested one
 * level deeper (inside "Image Group", i.e. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain) than the first pass
 * looked. Per Dani Rivett's scope note on the ticket, the badge shows on PLP and Wishlist (and
 * therefore Recently Viewed Full History, which already reuses the `plp` variation) and is
 * suppressed on Home — driven by `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge` below, the same table-driven
 * mechanism as every other variation decision in this file. Figma's own Home node still shows
 * the Tag layer un-hidden, contradicting that scope note — treating the confirmed written
 * requirement as authoritative over the file's possibly-stale layer visibility here, flagged
 * rather than silently picked.
 *
 * Badge count (confirmed after the above shipped, via a Dev Mode Connect Note on the separate
 * "Product Cards" Figma file — QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs, node 3448:35976 — distinct from the
 * design-system component-set file cited throughout this docblock): "only 1 product badge will
 * show up on these product cards - depending on the configured hierarchy, the highest priority
 * badge will be shown," with that priority logic owned by SFCC-225. This confirms `badge?:
 * string` (a single value, not a list) is the correct, final shape for this prop — not a
 * placeholder pending a possible future move to an array. SFCC-225's own already-merged SCAPI
 * hook writes `c_productBadges` as an array sorted by `badgePriorityOrder`, so whatever mapper
 * eventually feeds this prop (none exists yet — no page consumes this organism) just needs
 * `c_productBadges[0]?.productBadge`, not any re-sorting of its own.
 *
 * Hover image-swap on Home (same Dani-vs-AC contradiction as the Badge note above, resolved the
 * same direction): Dani's comment also says "we don't want the hover action (model photo) on
 * the homepage," but the AC update three days later frames the tile-image hover-swap as an
 * unconditional Core Component behaviour with no Home exclusion — and the code as first shipped
 * followed the AC, passing `swapOnHover` to `ZimmProductCardMedia` unconditionally with no
 * variation gate at all. Treated the comment as more authoritative than the AC text here too:
 * `VARIATION_CONFIG.showHoverImageSwap` now suppresses the swap for `home` specifically. This
 * is unrelated to, and does not affect, Home's own
 * `hoverRevealsPrice` — that is a separate mechanism (a style flag consumed by this organism's
 * own recipe), not `swapOnHover`.
 *
 * KNOWN GAP (postbuild doc/traceability audit, comment-only — no behaviour change): both
 * quotes above, from Dani's scope note (Jira comment 13880 on SFCC-236), truncate at the same
 * point. In full, her instruction is no badge and no hover-image-swap on "the Homepage or on
 * the Recently Viewed product carousel" — the Badge note above and this Hover image-swap note
 * each only implement and discuss the Homepage half. The Recently Viewed carousel half has no
 * code path in this file today: that surface is SFCC-83's rail component, which does not exist
 * yet and has no entry in the `ZimmProductCardVariation` union above. A rail caller reaching
 * for the closest existing option, `variation: 'plp'`, would get `showBadge: true` and
 * `showHoverImageSwap: true` from `VARIATION_CONFIG` — the opposite of what Dani asked for on
 * that surface. Whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to either add a dedicated `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry
 * for the rail (both flags `false`) or get explicit written confirmation on the ticket that the
 * suppression doesn't apply there — not assume `'plp'` already covers it.
 *
 * Fix I (SFCC-236, found via live mobile-device testing on this branch, same round that found
 * Fix H): multi-image cards did not respond to a real touch swipe at all — the slide indicator
 * rendered correctly (so the image data/gallery logic was fine), but swiping the image never
 * paged it. Root cause and CSS fix are `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s own Fix I (docblock point 2):
 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` was the one interactive region never lifted above the stretched-link
 * overlay, so a swipe gesture starting on the image landed on the invisible overlay `<a>` first
 * and never reached the real scroll container underneath. Lifting Media above the overlay fixes
 * the swipe, but has a side effect: a plain tap/click on the image used to "work" by landing on
 * that same overlay and navigating to the PDP — once Media sits on top, the tap no longer reaches
 * it, and Media itself had no click behaviour of its own. `handleMediaClick` below restores that
 * navigation deliberately, via `useHistory().push(href)` rather than depending on the overlay by
 * accident: this repo is pinned to react-router-dom v5.3.4 (`package.json`), which has no
 * `useNavigate` — `useHistory()` + `history.push()` is the correct v5 primitive, already
 * established in this codebase (`footer/index.tsx`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`,
 * `pages/product-detail/index.tsx`) and the same one the base SFCC `product-list` page itself
 * uses. `href` needed no new prop plumbing — this organism already destructures it from its own
 * base props (above) and previously only forwarded it to `ZimmProductCardContent`. The handler
 * guards against the two arrow buttons and the remove/close button — all real `<button>`
 * descendants of `ZimmProductCardMedia` — via `(event.target as HTMLElement).closest('button')`,
 * so paging and `onRemove` keep firing on their own and never also navigate. No custom drag-vs-tap
 * detection is needed for the swipe/tap split itself: browsers natively suppress the synthetic
 * `click` event after a real drag/scroll on the same element, so a swipe pages the gallery without
 * ever reaching this handler, while a plain tap (no movement) still fires it exactly as the old
 * overlay click did.
 */

/** Re-exported under this organism's own name so a page-level caller never has to reach into a
 *  molecule's type — the shape itself is Media's own `ZimmProductCardMediaImage`, not a
 *  redeclaration (a hand-copied duplicate would silently drift from its source). */
export type ZimmProductCardImage = ZimmProductCardMediaImage;

/** `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own already-derived heading-level type (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`,
 *  itself derived from `ZimmProductName`'s `as` prop) — read via `ComponentProps` off the
 *  component this organism actually forwards it to, rather than a hand-typed duplicate union. */
type ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductCardContent>['headingLevel'];

/**
 * Exported alongside `ZimmProductCardProps` (not just kept module-private) so a test/fixture can
 * build a properly *narrowed* per-variation props object — e.g.
 * `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation` — instead of a value typed as the
 * full union. This matters for real, not just for convenience: TypeScript's excess-property
 * check on a *union* target is weak (a property valid on any one member is not flagged as excess
 * on a fresh literal discriminated toward a different member), so proving "the wishlist-only
 * fields don't exist on Home" needs an assignment to Home's own narrow shape specifically, not to
 * the union alias — see index.test.tsx's `@ts-expect-error` cases and its overloaded
 * `buildCardProps` helper.
 */
export type ZimmProductCardBaseProps = {
  /** Stable per-card identifier. Not used for any layout/behavioural decision — exposed as a
   *  `data-product-id` attribute on the root element as a DOM hook for QA automation/analytics,
   *  the same kind of caller-facing marker `data-testid` already serves in this build's other
   *  components, without overloading that attribute's own testing-only convention. */
  id: string;
  /** PDP destination, pre-site-prefixed by the caller — forwarded straight to
   *  `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own `href` (see that component's own JSDoc on trust level). */
  href: string;
  name: string;
  headingLevel: ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel;
  primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage;
  hoverImage?: ZimmProductCardImage;
  images?: ZimmProductCardImage[];
  currentPrice?: string;
  originalPrice?: string;
  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
  isUnavailable?: boolean;
  /** Only meaningful when `isUnavailable` is true. See the module docblock for why this is not
   *  restricted to the `plp` variation at the type level. */
  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
  /**
   * Merchandiser-configured badge label (e.g. "Runway", "Exclusive"). Always a single value —
   * confirmed via a Figma Dev Mode Connect Note that only the single highest-priority badge is
   * ever shown, never a list (see the module docblock's "Badge count" note). Not restricted to
   * any variation at the type level, same reasoning as `onNotifyMe` above — whether it actually
   * renders is `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge`'s job (PLP/Wishlist show it, Home suppresses it; see
   * the module docblock's "Badge" note).
   */
  badge?: string;
};

export type ZimmProductCardPlpVariation = {
  variation: 'plp';
  onAddToBag?: () => void;
  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
};

export type ZimmProductCardHomeVariation = {
  variation: 'home';
  // No additions — Home never shows the bag, attributes, or size chips (see VARIATION_CONFIG).
};

export type ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation = {
  variation: 'wishlist';
  /** Required, not optional — the Wishlist AC always shows the attributes line. */
  colour: string;
  size: string;
  /** Required — a wishlist card with no way to remove itself is a spec violation. */
  onRemove: () => void;
  /** Bag is always visible for Wishlist per the confirmed matrix above. */
  onAddToBag?: () => void;
  /** Same trio `ZimmProductCardPlpVariation` declares, and for the same reason: confirmed via the
   *  real Figma Wishlist Hover instance (node 40002187:58458) during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual
   *  audit that Wishlist's hover reveal is a genuine, populated size-selector swap identical to
   *  PLP's — not a PLP-only affordance. `index.tsx`'s render body already forwarded these
   *  unconditionally to `ZimmProductCardContent` for every variation (via the
   *  `ZimmProductCardVariationFields` cast below); this type previously just didn't expose them
   *  to a Wishlist caller, which is what let the Wishlist story ship without ever populating them. */
  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
};

export type ZimmProductCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps &
  (ZimmProductCardPlpVariation | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation);

type ZimmProductCardVariation =
  | ZimmProductCardPlpVariation['variation']
  | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation['variation']
  | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation['variation'];

/**
 * Widened, not narrowed: every variation-specific field is optional here regardless of which
 * branch is actually active, purely so the component body below can destructure once with no
 * `if`/`switch` on `props.variation` — the extensibility AC requires every layout/visibility
 * decision to come from `VARIATION_CONFIG`, keyed by the discriminant, never a branching
 * statement. The exported `ZimmProductCardProps` discriminated union above is what actually
 * enforces correct usage at every call site (proven by the `@ts-expect-error` cases in
 * index.test.tsx) — this cast only relaxes internal access inside this file; it changes nothing
 * about what a caller may legally pass in.
 */
type ZimmProductCardVariationFields = Partial<
  Omit<ZimmProductCardPlpVariation, 'variation'> &
    Omit<ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation, 'variation'> &
    Omit<ZimmProductCardHomeVariation, 'variation'>
>;

type ZimmProductCardVariationConfig = {
  showBag: boolean;
  showAttributes: boolean;
  showSizeChips: boolean;
  /** PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default and hides on hover. */
  hoverHidesPrice: boolean;
  /** Home only: price is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
  hoverRevealsPrice: boolean;
  /** PLP/Wishlist: the size-chip picker is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
  hoverRevealsSizeSelector: boolean;
  showRemove: boolean;
  /** PLP only (found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): Figma's Mobile Card-content
   *  instance has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`, unlike Desktop and unlike
   *  Wishlist's own Mobile instance (bag stays visible there on every breakpoint). A viewport-
   *  width concern, not a hover one — see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rule. */
  hideBagOnMobile: boolean;
  /** Wishlist only (found during the follow-up full-sweep visual audit against every variant x
   *  state node): unlike PLP's unconditional `hideBagOnMobile`, Wishlist's Mobile Card-content
   *  instance shows the bag icon when available (`40002187:58470`) and hides it
   *  (`Icons` frame `hidden="true"`) only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
   *  `hideBagOnMobile`, and combined with it (not replacing it) in the `bagHiddenOnMobile`
   *  derivation below, since the two are mutually exclusive per variation today but there is no
   *  reason to assume that stays true forever. */
  hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: boolean;
  /** Shown on PLP/Wishlist, suppressed on Home — see the module docblock's "Badge" note. */
  showBadge: boolean;
  /**
   * Allows `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s primary/hover image crossfade for this variation. Suppressed
   * on Home per Dani Rivett's scope note, overriding the AC's unconditional framing — see the
   * module docblock's "Hover image-swap on Home" note. `false` here means a supplied
   * `hoverImage` is simply never swapped to, regardless of pointer capability.
   */
  showHoverImageSwap: boolean;
};

/**
 * The extensibility AC's actual mechanism: every layout/visibility decision this organism makes
 * reads from this table, keyed by `variation` — adding a future variation means adding a union
 * member above and one row here, touching no JSX. `index.tsx`'s render body contains no
 * `switch`/`if` on `props.variation` anywhere (verify with
 * `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` — zero hits).
 */
const VARIATION_CONFIG: Record<ZimmProductCardVariation, ZimmProductCardVariationConfig> = {
  home: {
    showBag: false,
    showAttributes: false,
    showSizeChips: false,
    hoverHidesPrice: false,
    hoverRevealsPrice: true,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: false,
    showRemove: false,
    hideBagOnMobile: false,
    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
    showBadge: false,
    showHoverImageSwap: false,
  },
  plp: {
    showBag: true,
    showAttributes: false,
    showSizeChips: true,
    hoverHidesPrice: true,
    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
    showRemove: false,
    hideBagOnMobile: true,
    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
    showBadge: true,
    showHoverImageSwap: true,
  },
  wishlist: {
    showBag: true,
    showAttributes: true,
    showSizeChips: true,
    hoverHidesPrice: true,
    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
    showRemove: true,
    hideBagOnMobile: false,
    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: true,
    showBadge: true,
    showHoverImageSwap: true,
  },
};

const messages = defineMessages({
  // Interpolated with the product name, matching ZimmProductPrice's WAS/NOW pattern — Media's
  // own `removeLabel` prop is a plain string, so the interpolation happens here, at the one call
  // site that actually knows the product name.
  removeFromWishlist: {
    id: 'product_card.remove.from_wishlist',
    defaultMessage: 'Remove {name} from wishlist',
  },
});

const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCard';

/**
 * Organism — the full product card, composing `ZimmProductCardMedia` and `ZimmProductCardContent`
 * across the `home` / `plp` / `wishlist` variations. See the module docblock above for the
 * confirmed Figma variation matrix and this component's own recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) for
 * the stretched-link and hover-reveal mechanics that live entirely in CSS, not in this render
 * body — both children are always rendered in full, with every one of their own sub-parts; CSS
 * alone decides what is visible for a given variation and pointer capability.
 *
 * @param props see `ZimmProductCardProps` — a discriminated union on `variation`.
 */
export const ZimmProductCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
  const {
    id,
    href,
    name,
    headingLevel,
    primaryImage,
    hoverImage,
    images,
    currentPrice,
    originalPrice,
    isPriceLoading,
    isUnavailable,
    onNotifyMe,
    badge,
    variation,
  } = props;

  const { onAddToBag, sizeChipValues, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect, colour, size, onRemove } =
    props as ZimmProductCardVariationFields;

  const intl = useIntl();
  const history = useHistory();
  const config = VARIATION_CONFIG[variation];

  // Both conditions required — an organism that sets isUnavailable without a real callback
  // should not show a dead notify-me button. Mirrors ZimmProductCardContent's own
  // showNotifyMeButton co-requirement.
  const showNotifyMe = Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe);

  // Fix C (SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): confirmed against the real Figma Default+Hover
  // instances for every variation × Unavailable=True (including the Mobile/no-hover variants,
  // which show the only state a touch pointer ever sees) that `isUnavailable` suppresses the
  // size-selector hover-swap entirely — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so
  // price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own hover-reveals-price
  // behaviour is untouched by this — Home's Unavailable Hover reference (node 40002163:39990)
  // still reveals price on hover exactly as the in-stock case does; only the PLP/Wishlist
  // hide-and-swap needs suppressing.
  //
  // Suppressing `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` alone is not enough to reproduce that reference: it
  // only stops the organism adding its OWN hide/reveal pair, which leaves the size-chip wrapper
  // at Content's own natural (visible) default — briefly shipped that way mid-fix and caught by
  // re-checking the real Storybook render against Figma, which confirms size chips stay hidden
  // in BOTH states when unavailable, not just "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
  // carries that permanent hide separately, unconditional (not gated by hover-capability at all —
  // this isn't a pointer-type concern, unlike everything else in this recipe).
  //
  // Follow-up (full-sweep visual audit against every variant x state node, not just the sampled
  // set the first pass checked): `sizeSelectorUnavailable` ALSO drives a mobile-only price hide
  // in the recipe now (Fix F) — confirmed via `get_metadata` that Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable
  // hide price and show notify-me in its place (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`), the OPPOSITE
  // of Desktop's additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover). Nothing
  // extra is computed here for it — the recipe reads the same `sizeSelectorUnavailable` boolean
  // for both the size-chip permanent-hide and this new price rule, since both only ever apply to
  // the same PLP/Wishlist-and-unavailable case.
  const hoverHidesPrice = config.hoverHidesPrice && !isUnavailable;
  const hoverRevealsSizeSelector = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && !isUnavailable;
  const sizeSelectorUnavailable = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && Boolean(isUnavailable);

  // Fix G (same follow-up audit): Wishlist-only. `hideBagOnMobile` alone only covers PLP's own
  // unconditional mobile hide; Wishlist's bag stays visible on mobile UNLESS unavailable
  // (`40002187:58470` vs `40002187:58473`). Combined into one boolean here rather than exposing
  // both conditions to the recipe — it only needs to know "hide this on mobile for this render",
  // not why.
  const bagHiddenOnMobile = config.hideBagOnMobile || (config.hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable && Boolean(isUnavailable));

  const removeLabel = config.showRemove ? intl.formatMessage(messages.removeFromWishlist, { name }) : undefined;
  const resolvedBadge = config.showBadge ? badge : undefined;

  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE, {
    hoverHidesPrice,
    hoverRevealsPrice: config.hoverRevealsPrice,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
    // Same Fix C audit: notify-me is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default,
    // revealed on hover/focus-visible — every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it
    // appearing only there) but unconditionally visible on touch (every Mobile Unavailable
    // reference — the only state a touch pointer ever sees, per the "Mobile has no Hover variant"
    // finding — shows it plainly, with no hover to reveal it). This flag is deliberately keyed off
    // `showNotifyMe` itself, not `variation`: the confirmed behaviour is identical across all
    // three variations, and the recipe's selector simply matches nothing when notify-me isn't
    // mounted at all.
    hoverRevealsNotifyMe: showNotifyMe,
    hideBagOnMobile: bagHiddenOnMobile,
  });

  // Fix I — see the module docblock's own "Fix I" paragraph for the full narrative. Guards the
  // two arrow buttons and the remove/close button (all real <button> descendants of
  // ZimmProductCardMedia) so paging/onRemove keep firing on their own and never also navigate.
  // Fix L (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a real <a> lets the
  // browser handle Cmd/Ctrl-click (new tab), Shift-click (new window), and non-primary-button
  // clicks natively — this handler only ever replaces the in-page navigation an UNMODIFIED,
  // primary-button click used to reach via the stretched-link overlay (see Fix I). Bailing out on
  // any of those instead of forcing an in-tab `history.push` regardless of what the shopper
  // actually asked for; a no-op here is a real gap (it doesn't open a new tab the way a real link
  // would) but is strictly better than silently overriding an explicit "open elsewhere" signal.
  const handleMediaClick = (event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>): void => {
    const target = event.target as HTMLElement;
    if (target.closest('button')) return;
    if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.shiftKey || event.altKey || event.button !== 0) return;
    history.push(href);
  };

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-testid="product-card" data-product-id={id}>
      <ZimmProductCardMedia
        primaryImage={primaryImage}
        hoverImage={hoverImage}
        images={images}
        swapOnHover={config.showHoverImageSwap && Boolean(hoverImage)}
        showControls
        badge={resolvedBadge}
        onRemove={onRemove}
        removeLabel={removeLabel}
        onClick={handleMediaClick}
      />
      <ZimmProductCardContent
        name={name}
        headingLevel={headingLevel}
        href={href}
        currentPrice={currentPrice}
        originalPrice={originalPrice}
        isPriceLoading={isPriceLoading}
        showAttributes={config.showAttributes}
        colour={colour}
        size={size}
        showBag={config.showBag}
        isUnavailable={isUnavailable}
        onAddToBag={onAddToBag}
        showSizeChips={config.showSizeChips}
        sizeChipValues={sizeChipValues}
        selectedSizeChipValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
        onSizeChipSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
        showNotifyMe={showNotifyMe}
        onNotifyMe={onNotifyMe}
      />
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

export default ZimmProductCard;

import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';

/**
 * Shared DOM-contract constants for the ZimmProductCard organism and its composed molecules
 * (ZimmProductCardMedia, ZimmProductCardContent) — defined once here so every producer (the JSX
 * that stamps a `data-card-slot` attribute) and consumer (the organism's own recipe selectors,
 * plus this component family's test suites) reads the same value instead of each independently
 * retyping it. Same pattern, smaller scale, as `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`.
 */

/**
 * The ten `data-card-slot` attribute values that wire the organism's hover/reveal CSS
 * (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) to specific descendant DOM nodes. `media` / `badge` / `close` /
 * `carousel` / `indicator` are stamped by `ZimmProductCardMedia`; `content` / `bag` / `price` /
 * `sizeChips` / `notifyMe` by `ZimmProductCardContent`. Do not rename a value here without
 * checking both molecules' own docblocks, which document what each slot is for.
 */
export const CARD_SLOT = {
  media: 'media',
  badge: 'badge',
  close: 'close',
  carousel: 'carousel',
  indicator: 'indicator',
  content: 'content',
  bag: 'bag',
  price: 'price',
  sizeChips: 'sizeChips',
  notifyMe: 'notifyMe',
} as const;

348	      // specificity than Media's own single-class rule, so a competing `position` value declared

386	        zIndex: 1,

388	      },
389

391	      // half of each flag below is what makes a touch/no-hover pointer see the *default* state

437	        ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {

439	          // the unconditional block above, where it used to live — Home's Mobile reference

441	          // reveal a price hidden unconditionally like the original shape did. Confirmed live as

455	            clipPath: 'none',

487	          },

502	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
503	            position: 'absolute',
504	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
505	          },

582	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {

584	          clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
585	        },
586	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
587	          display: 'flex',
588	          clipPath: 'none',
589	        },

591	        // above): re-enables the arrow buttons' hit-testing only once genuinely revealed.
592	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
593	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
594	        },
595	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
596	          display: 'flex',
597	          clipPath: 'none',
598	        },
599	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
600	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
601	        },
602	      },

604	      // 5. PLP-only bag-icon mobile hide — see docblock point 5. A separate, sibling media-query

626	      // `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` above never had this problem because it was always written as a
627	      // single key with every contributing condition spread INSIDE it — this block now follows
